To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have found a new class of gauge actions, which are constructed to conserve the topology and which are suitable for numerical studies of QCD, (2) these actions are very useful for the simulation of the static potential and the determination of r0 and (3) the actions are also useful for numerical studies of dynamical quarks and the overlap operator, where the condition number of its kernel can be reduced

we have constructed a new family of gauge actions, which are constructed in a way that the occurrence of very small plaquette values, which is known to be the main obstacle for simulations in the e regime, is strongly suppressed.

we have constructed gauge actions which suppress small plaquette values, that these actions are stable and that the suppression of small plaquettes leads to improved performance in the local HMI algorithm, as compared to standard plaquette and Symanzik actions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
gauge actions for lattice simulations in the e-regim e and with the implementation of the local HMC in the presence of such actions.
a systematic study of the topological properties of gauge actions, which conserve the topological charges in a numerical simulation.
the development of a novel lattice action, which is based on the admissibility conditions of topological charge conservation, which we test in the e-regim.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the topologically conserving gauge actions are not superior in any of these aspects.
all these quantities are improved compared to the standard Wilson plaquette action.
the topologically conserving gauge actions are not advantageous for numerical studies of the static potential and the physical scale r 0.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the topological charge is conserved in the simulations, but the suppression of small plaquettes is not sufficient to reduce the condition number of overlap significantly.
the topological conserving gauge actions are very well suited for numerical simulations in the e-regim e and with dynamical quark action.
the topological conserving actions are promising for simulations at small lattice spacings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the admissibility conditions can be used to construct gauge actions which are competitive with the Wilson plaquette action and the tree-level improved Symanzik gauge action.
the admissibility constraint is a very powerful tool to construct gauge actions with a very small condition number and a large acceptance rate in the local HMG algorithm.
the topological charge conserving action leads to a significant reduction in the acceptance rate, which makes it impractical for the simulation of QCD with dynamical quark flavors.
